name: AvatarGroup
purpose: Shows several people or entities associated with the same record as a compact overlapping stack of Avatars, collapsing whatever doesn't fit into a '+N' count.
neverUseFor: A single person — use Avatar directly
A full member/roster list where every name matters — use Table or List with one Avatar per row, not a collapsed stack
Decorative clusters not tied to real people/entities on the record
rationale: AvatarGroup collapses several people tied to one record into a compact overlapping stack with a '+N' overflow, so tables and cards stay scannable. Every child is an Avatar at the group's size, so heights stay on the same semantic.size rungs; names are exposed through per-avatar Tooltips and a labelled group rather than extra focus stops. Hovering an avatar lifts and scales only that avatar (component.avatarGroup.hover-lift/hover-scale, aliasing the generic semantic.transform.lift.s and scale.s — approved 2026-09-24); its neighbours never move, and under prefers-reduced-motion nothing moves at all.

mayExtendLocally: Choose how many avatars are visible before collapsing into '+N'
Link the '+N' count or the group to a full roster view at the usage site
mustEscalateToDS: Changing the overlap distance, ring border or overflow treatment
Making individual avatars focusable or interactive
Mixing avatar sizes inside one group

anatomy.description: Root flex container. Stacks child avatars with a negative overlap and renders them in reverse DOM order so the first item in `avatars` sits visually on top.
Wraps each rendered Avatar to apply the overlap offset and the page-color separation ring.

The '+N' indicator for avatars beyond `max`. Rendered only when `avatars.length` exceeds `max`, always last — rightmost, on top of the stack, overlapping the last visible avatar. Neutral gray, never Avatar's tinted fill/text.

props.name: avatars
props.description: The people/entities to display, in the order they should stack — first entry renders on top. Each item maps 1:1 to Avatar's `label`/`src`.

props.name: max
props.description: Maximum number of avatars to render before collapsing the rest into a '+N' overflow indicator. Unset shows every avatar.

props.name: size
props.description: Physical size applied to every avatar and the overflow indicator. Shares Avatar's field scale (s=24, m=32, l=40).

height.note: Matches Avatar's height exactly — same semantic.size.{s,m,l} rungs, since every child is an Avatar at the group's size.

width.note: Width hugs content: (visible avatar count) x size, minus the overlap between each pair. Not fixed — driven by `avatars.length` and `max`.

notes: Each avatar is wrapped in Tooltip (see contracts/components/Tooltip.json), showing that person's name on hover — mouse only, since individual avatars carry no tabindex/focus behavior (keyboardNav stays []).
The '+N' overflow indicator is also wrapped in Tooltip, listing the hidden names (comma-separated) — no longer presentational-only.

motion: CSS transitions/animations: neutralised by the global prefers-reduced-motion rule

properties.name: overflow
properties.description: Shows the +N item (code renders it when avatars exceed max).

figma.structure: Avatar instances in avatar-group-item rings (2px, fill/page). The 8px overlap (avatarGroup.overlap) is modeled without a negative gap: every item after the first sits in a slot 8px narrower than itself, offset 8px left, so it paints over the previous one and the group's width matches code (m, 3 avatars: 92px). The hover lift is a motion effect, not modeled.
